Q: why is php generating different hmac-sha256 compared to online generators? A:

CryptoJS.HmacSHA256 in JavaScript produces binary hash value

While hash_hmac() in PHP will produce hash value as hexadecimal. If you pass the 4th parameter as true to hash_hmac(), you will get binary hash value. From the PHP documentation: https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.hash-hmac.php:

binary

When set to true, outputs raw binary data. false outputs lowercase hexits.

So the hash_hmac() with the 4th parameter set to true will match the value produced by CryptoJS.HmacSHA256.

In addition, you could also transform hexadecimal hash in PHP to binary with hex2bin and get the same result:

hex2bin(hash_hmac('sha256', $data, $secret)) == hash_hmac('sha256', $data, $secret, true)

Q: How can I create a virtual environment with Python 3? A:

virtualenv is the tool of choice for Python 2, while venv handles the task in Python 3.

Yet, you can create the virtual environment for Python 3 using any of them.

Using venv

python3 -m venv virtualenvname

Command syntax:

/path/to/python3 -m venv /path/to/directory/virtual_env_name

Using virtualenv

virtualenv -p python3 virtualenvname

Command Syntax:

virtualenv -p /path/to/python3 /path/to/directory/virtual_env_name

Activate the virtual environment

On Linux, Unix or macOS, using the terminal or Bash shell:

source /path/to/venv/bin/activate

E.g., source virtualenvname/bin/activate

On Unix or macOS, using the C shell shell (executable csh):

source /path/to/venv/bin/activate.csh

On Unix or macOS, using the Fish shell:

source /path/to/venv/bin/activate.fish

On Windows using the Command Prompt:

path\to\venv\Scripts\activate.bat

On Windows using PowerShell:

path\to\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

Deactivating the virtual environment

On Linux, Unix or macOS, using the terminal or Bash shell:

deactivate

On Windows using the Command Prompt:

path\to\venv\Scripts\deactivate.bat

On Windows using PowerShell:

deactivate

This answer is for those who may use a different operating system.

Q: Time difference between day and time A:

tl;dr

Use Duration to calculate time elapsed between a pair of moments such as ZonedDateTime objects.

Duration.between(
    now ,  // ZonedDateTime.now( ZoneId.of( "Africa/Tunis" ) )
    zdt    // now.toLocalDate().with( TemporalAccessors.next( DayOfWeek.WEDNESDAY ) ).atTime( LocalTime.of( 9 , 0 ) ).atZone( ZoneId.of( "Africa/Tunis" ) )
)

Avoid legacy date-time classes

Never use the terribly flawed legacy date-time classes such as Date, Calendar, SimpleDateFormat, etc.

java.time

Use on the modern java.time classes built into Java 8+.

DayOfWeek & LocalTime

DayTime1 = "Wed 09:00:00"

Do not manage that information as text. We have classes for both data types.

DayOfWeek dow = DayOfWeek.WEDNESDAY ;
LocalTime time = LocalTime.of( 9 , 0 );  // 9 AM.

Capture the current moment as seen in your expected/desired time zone.

ZoneId zone = ZoneId.of( "Asia/Tokyo" ) ;  // Or `ZoneId.systemDefault()`.
ZonedDateTime now = ZonedDateTime.now( zone ) ;

Extract the date, and move to the next date with your desired day-of-week. Use a TemporalAdjuster implementation found in TemporalAdjusters (plural) utility class.

LocalDate today = now.toLocalDate() ;
LocalDate dateAfter = today.with( TemporalAccessors.next( dow ) ) ;

Apply your desired time and zone to determine a moment, a point on the timeline.

ZonedDateTime zdt = ZonedDateTime.of( dateAfter , time , zone ) ;

Be aware that your desired time on that date in that zone may not exist. The ZonedDateTime class adjusts as necessary. See Javadoc for adjustment algorithm.

Calculate time to elapse between your two moments.

Duration duration = Duration.between( now , zdt ) ;
